title: Dancing Kaomoji ┏(・o・)┛: Copy & Paste Dance Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste dancing kaomoji: arm-swinging dancers like ┏(・o・)┛ and ♪┏(・o･)┛♪, wiggling (~˘▾˘)~ moves, party dances and kaomoji dancing with music notes.
hero_tagline: Text faces mid-move, swinging their arms, shuffling side to side or dancing to a few music notes. Tap one to copy the whole move.
intro: A dancing kaomoji shows movement with the arms. Box-drawing corners like ┏ ┛ and ┗ ┓ put one arm up and one down, so writing ┏(・o・)┛ and then ┗(・o・)┓ looks like a dancer switching sides. Tildes ~ trail behind a face that is wiggling, and ♪ ♫ notes say there is a song playing. Some longer lines are a short dance routine in one string. People use them to celebrate good news, react to a song drop, or hype up a party chat. For faces singing or playing instruments rather than dancing, see the music kaomoji page linked below.

sections.label: Arm Dances
sections.intro: The box-drawing corners ┏ ┛ ┗ ┓ are the arms, bent at the elbow. Pair two that mirror each other to show the switch.

sections.label: Wiggle Dances
sections.intro: Tildes show a body swaying. The ~ on one side means the dancer is leaning that way.

sections.label: With Music
sections.intro: Notes around the face put a song behind the move. ♪ is a single note and ♫ is a pair of beamed notes.

sections.label: Party Dances
sections.intro: Bigger, louder moves for a win, a birthday or the weekend. ヾ and ノ are hands thrown in the air.

faq.q: How do I make a kaomoji look like it is dancing?
faq.a: Send two mirrored faces one after the other, such as ┏(・o・)┛ then ┗(・o・)┓. The arms swap sides, which reads as a dance move. Adding ♪ before or after the face tells people there is music.
They are box-drawing characters, made for drawing tables and frames in plain text. In a kaomoji the corner shape looks like an arm bent at the elbow, one raised and one lowered.

faq.q: What is the difference between a dancing kaomoji and the dancing emoji?
faq.a: The 💃 and 🕺 emoji are pictures drawn by each platform's emoji font, so they look different on each phone. A dancing kaomoji is built from ordinary text characters and keeps the same shape wherever the font has those characters.
